content:
devon: Heads-up — after rolling attn-optimized-v2 + quant profile update this morning, we've got a sustained drop in prefix cache hit-rate on prod gpus.

devon: P99 generation latency jumped ~18% on mid-length prompts (seq 256-512) and unit cost up ~12%.

sanjay: Saw the same. Quick numbers from perf-ci: prefix_cache.hit_rate by prompt_len bucket:
- 0-128: 94% -> 92%
- 129-512: 89% -> 67%  <-- big regression
- 513+: 76% -> 74%

sanjay: root cause hypothesis: attn kernel variant changed key layout for KV-cache (reordered KV blocks) and our key canonicalization didn't tolerate the new block order, so warmup misses for mid-lengths where kv split boundary differs.

maya: Any smoking logs? can we diff cache keys for same prompt before/after?

sanjay: yesss — captured a few keys. Example diff:
```
# before (legacy kernel)
key: sha1|tok:0000abcd|len:260|kvv:chunk0
# after (v2 kernel)
key: sha1|tok:0000abcd|len:260|kvv:chunk0:orderB
```

sanjay: The kernel now appends a variant suffix when kv layout crosses an internal block boundary. That changes the key string and prevents a hit.

ellie: Oof. That explains mid-length skew. Short prompts never hit block boundary; long prompts always add suffix consistently, so only the middle bucket flips.

build-bot: perf-ci posted artifacts: https://ci.redwood/run/199876/attn-v2/prefetch-flame.html :eyes:

devon: Repro steps I used:
```
# collect traces
redwood-trace --service=runtime --tag=attn-v2 --out=/tmp/trace.pb
# sample keys
python tools/kv_key_dump.py --trace /tmp/trace.pb --out keys.txt
```

maya: Immediate mitigation options?

sanjay: Short-term: enable PREF_CACHE_COMPAT=legacy on rollout for attn-optimized-v2 so runtime normalizes keys to legacy form until we ship a canonicalizer.

ellie: Will that require restart? we can flip via feature-flag to avoid full rollback.

sanjay: Yes, it's a runtime feature-flag toggle. Command:
```
redwood-runtime update-flag --name=prefix_key_compat --value=legacy --scope=region:prod
```

devon: Patch plan for tomorrow:
1) Add key canonicalizer that normalizes out kernel-internal suffixes (sha256 of canonical token list + model_version + normalized_layout)
2) Add unit tests with fuzz keys from different kernels
3) Add metric prefix_cache.normalized_fraction to monitor
4) Backfill keys for hot prompts via a short-lived prefetch job

maya: Longer-term: can we avoid exposing kernel internal layout in the key at all? kernel should provide a stability token rather than raw layout.

sanjay: Agreed. I'll add a kernel API change request: get_kv_stable_id() so runtime uses that instead of layout string.

ellie: Who wants to own the quick flag flip and rollout? I'll do the rollout and monitor dashboards.

devon: TY. @ellie please also add an alert for prefix_cache.hit_rate < 75% on 129-512 bucket.

ellie: on it. I'll do a canary change to 10% of traffic first.

maya: After flip: re-run perf job and paste before/after numbers.

ellie: Update — toggled prefix_key_compat=legacy on 10% canary at 09:42. Initial look: bucket 129-512 hit-rate went 67% -> 86% on canary. p99 latency improved ~12%.

devon: Nice. Roll forward to 100% when green.

ellie: Rolling to 100% now. :rocket: 

build-bot: deploy success: runtime-2026.03.18-flag-roll.json

sanjay: Postmortem action items:
- formal kernel compatibility contract (sanjay)
- implement key canonicalizer (devon)
- add normalized_fraction metric + alert (maya)
- prefetch job for top-1000 prompts (ellie)

maya: Anything else? also consider adding batching heuristic change detection — batch boundaries can also change KV block splits.

devon: Good call. Add a telemetry tag for batching profile per model version.

ellie: Closing loop: will post follow-up notes and bench artifacts to eng-runtime channel thread.

devon: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
